title: Finite pushforward preserves and reflects finite presentation near a singleton fibre
statement: Let $p:T\to U$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] that is of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $t\in T$ and $u=p(t)$, and assume $p^{-1}(\{u\})=\{t\}$. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal M$ on $T$ [pqf-def-coherent], $\mathcal M$ is of finite presentation on a neighbourhood of $t$ if and only if $p_*\mathcal M$ is of finite presentation on a neighbourhood of $u$ [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Moreover, $\mathcal M_t$ is finitely presented over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ if and only if $(p_*\mathcal M)_u$ is finitely presented over $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Here $p_*\mathcal M$ is the Zariski direct image: for an open $V\subseteq U$, $(p_*\mathcal M)(V)=\mathcal M(p^{-1}V)$ with $\mathcal O_U(V)$ acting through $p^\sharp(V):\mathcal O_U(V)\to\mathcal O_T(p^{-1}V)$; the stalks and their scalar actions are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk].

source.place: Tag 057T, proof paragraph beginning “Using Descent, Lemma 03C4 ...”; stalk paragraph using More on Morphisms Tag 0A1H.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-singleton-fibre-localization] to $p,t,\mathcal M$: its hypotheses are finiteness, the given singleton fibre, and quasi-coherence. For every neighbourhood $W\ni t$ it supplies an open $V_0\ni u$ with $p^{-1}V_0\subseteq W$. Refine $V_0$ to an affine neighbourhood $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The same singleton-fibre lemma supplies the canonical $\mathcal O_{U,u}$-linear isomorphism $\theta:(p_*\mathcal M)_u\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal M_t$, with scalars on the right restricted along $p_t^\sharp$.

source.place: Tag 057T, neighbourhood and final stalk comparisons; More on Morphisms 05B8(1),(4).

proof.text: For each affine open $V\subseteq U$, put $p_V:p^{-1}V\to V$. This is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]: affine opens in $V$ have the same affine inverse images and finite section-ring maps as for $p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] all these affine section-ring maps are finitely presented, so $p_V$ is locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The restriction $\mathcal M|_{p^{-1}V}$ is quasi-coherent by its affine-local definition [pqf-def-coherent]. Thus both new global direct-image lemmas apply to $p_V$ and this restriction. Its direct image equals $(p_*\mathcal M)|_V$: on every open $D\subseteq V$ both are $\mathcal M(p^{-1}D)$, with the same structural scalar map. Consequently [lem-trf-finite-pushforward-preserves-finite-presentation] gives the forward finite-presentation implication on these opens, and [lem-trf-finite-pushforward-reflects-finite-presentation] gives the reverse implication.

Finite presentation restricts to smaller opens, since its local finite-free presentations in [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] still present the restricted module. If $\mathcal M$ has finite presentation on $W\ni t$, choose $V$ as in Step 1 and apply the forward implication of Step 2. If $p_*\mathcal M$ has finite presentation on $V_0\ni u$, choose affine $u\in V\subseteq V_0$ by Step 1 and apply the reverse implication of Step 2. The inverse image $p^{-1}V$ contains $t$. This proves the neighbourhood equivalence.

source.place: Tag 057T, neighbourhood equivalence; restriction of local presentations.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-finite-singleton-fibre-stalk-ring], $p_t^\sharp:\mathcal O_{U,u}\to\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is finite and finitely presented, using exactly the finite, finitely presented and singleton-fibre hypotheses of the item. Apply [lem-trf-finite-extension-module-finite-presentation] to this map and $\mathcal M_t$: finite presentation over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is equivalent to finite presentation over $\mathcal O_{U,u}$. Use the linear isomorphism $\theta$ of Step 1 to replace the latter module by $(p_*\mathcal M)_u$. Explicitly, compose the final surjection of a finite presentation with $\theta$ or $\theta^{-1}$; its kernel stays the same, so exactness and the two finite ranks are unchanged [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: Tag 057T, final stalk paragraph; More on Morphisms 05B8(2),(3); Algebra 0564.
